about: Pick a niche: 127's crowd scores for each business type (copied from research/crowd.json, the library thread's file; leads.test.js checks the copy still matches), plus a plain label, the words members use for it, the kind (b2b: you sell to businesses; home: you sell to households; online: not tied to a city), and what to count nearby on OpenStreetMap (buyers, partners who could refer people, or places to source from). Scores are our judgment, not data.

count.what: gyms and fitness studios

crowd.note: Flagship. A sample Reel first. Pitch in the fall: January is when gyms sign up the most new members.
not_yet: Don't buy a camera before your first paid client. Your phone shoots Reels.
Don't edit for weeks for free. One sample per gym is enough.
Don't pitch chains. Owner-run gyms decide in one visit.

count.what: plumbers, HVAC companies, roofers and electricians

crowd.buyer: Home service contractors (plumbing, HVAC, roofing, electrical)
crowd.note: Sell "never miss a call", not AI. Pitch before their busy season: spring for cooling and roofing, fall for heating.
not_yet: Don't buy phone software before your first yes. Set it up on their account.
Don't say AI in your first message. Say you'll make sure they never miss a call.
Don't build anything custom yet. The setup is the product.

reviews.label: More Google reviews for local shops
reviews.pack: More Google reviews for local shops

count.what: salons, barbershops, nail salons, spas and auto shops

crowd.note: Measurable: the review count goes up or it doesn't.
not_yet: Don't buy, gate or trade for reviews. It breaks Google's rules and the FTC's.
Don't build a dashboard. A one-page monthly report is enough.
Don't pitch chains. Owner-run shops decide in one visit.

count.what: trades, auto shops, salons, dentists and law firms

crowd.note: A mock homepage is instant spec work.
not_yet: Don't build your own portfolio site first. The mock homepages are your portfolio.
Don't learn a new site builder before your first sale.
Don't quote custom features. Sell one clear package.

social.label: Social media for restaurants and cafes
social.pack: Social media for restaurants and cafes

count.what: restaurants, cafes, bakeries and bars

crowd.note: Thin margins and high churn. Lead with one clear result a month.
not_yet: Don't sell 30 posts a month first. Start with one week they can see.
Don't buy a camera. A phone and good window light are enough.
Don't chase chains. Owner-run spots decide in one visit.

count.what: real estate agents and property managers who could refer people to you

crowd.note: Recurring. Spring, move season and the holidays are the peaks.
not_yet: Don't buy commercial equipment before your fifth regular.
Don't build a website before your first 3 regulars. A Google profile and a price sheet are enough.
Don't fill your week with one-time deep cleans. Aim for recurring.

count.what: car dealers and auto shops who could refer people to you

off_season.play: Sell interior details, holiday gift cards, and fleet or dealership work that runs all year.

crowd.note: Cash this week.
not_yet: Don't buy a water tank and trailer before you've booked a full week.
Don't pay for a coating course before your first 10 details.
Don't design a logo before your first yes.

count.what: schools (where the parents are)

off_season.play: Sell summer catch-up packages and book fall slots now.

crowd.note: Safety rules with minors come first: parents book, and sessions happen where a parent can see.
not_yet: Don't hand out flyers at a school without the school's okay.
Don't take on more subjects than you can teach well.
Don't message students directly. Talk to parents.

count.what: vets, pet groomers and pet stores who could refer people to you

crowd.note: Trust first. Summer and the holidays are the busiest weeks for sitting.
not_yet: Don't skip the meet and greet.
Don't take dogs you can't handle in your first month.
Don't pay for a booking app before you have 3 regulars.

count.what: restaurants, real estate agents, boutiques, salons and med spas

crowd.note: Needs gear. Start with what you own.
not_yet: Don't buy a new camera before your first paid shoot.
Don't shoot weddings first. Start with local business shoots.
Don't take a week to edit. Deliver within 3 days.

crowd.note: Online flagship: a sample clip first.
not_yet: Don't buy a lighting kit before your first paid clip.
Don't pitch the biggest brands first. Small stores answer.
Don't chase followers. Brands pay for the clip, not your audience.

count.what: real estate agents and property managers who could refer people to you

off_season.play: Sell snow removal and leaf cleanups, and book spring mowing now at this year's price.

crowd.note: Off season November to March up north.
not_yet: Don't buy a trailer or a riding mower before your tenth regular.
Don't take jobs across town. Same street first.
Don't apply fertilizer or weed killer for pay before checking your state's license rule.

count.what: storefront restaurants and cafes, and property managers

off_season.play: Book spring jobs now, and offer storefront window cleaning or holiday light installs.

crowd.note: Off season up north.
not_yet: Don't buy a hot-water machine before your tenth job.
Don't blast roofs or soft siding at full pressure. Learn soft washing first.
Don't let wash water run into storm drains before you check your city's rules.

crowd.buyer: People who want one specific result
crowd.note: Needs proof first. January is the busiest month to start.
not_yet: Don't build a course before you've coached 3 people.
Don't pay for ads before you have a story you're allowed to share.
Don't pick a crowd wider than one kind of person and one result.

count.what: thrift and second-hand shops to buy from

crowd.note: Inventory risk. Buy small and sell fast.
not_yet: Don't buy in bulk before you've flipped 10 items.
Don't list on every site at once. Start with one.
Don't hold an item past 60 days. Drop the price and move it.

crowd.note: Crowded. Planners peak in December and January.
not_yet: Don't make 50 templates before one sells.
Don't pay for ads before a listing sells on its own.
Don't copy a bestseller. Trademark and copyright rules apply.

crowd.note: Months to a first $1.
not_yet: Don't buy tools or a course before your first 30 uploads.
Don't use music or clips you don't have the rights to.
Don't count on ad money for months.

count.what: real estate agents, property managers and storefront shops who could refer people to you

off_season.play: Book spring window cleanings now with a deposit, and keep a storefront route every 2 weeks going through winter.

crowd.note: Spring and fall peaks; slow in winter up north.
not_yet: Don't buy a water-fed pole system before your tenth regular customer. Start with squeegees and ladders.
Don't take third-story or roof work before you have liability insurance, the right gear and practice on lower floors.
Don't raise a ladder near power lines, and never use a metal one near them.

count.what: pool supply stores, real estate agents and HOAs and community managers who could refer people to you

off_season.play: Where pools close for winter, sell closings in October and November, then book spring openings with a deposit from December. Where pools stay open all year, keep the weekly route full.

crowd.note: Pools in places like Florida, Phoenix and San Diego stay open all year. Up north most pools open in May or June and close in the fall.
not_yet: Don't repair pumps, heaters or pipes before you check your state's contractor license rule.
Don't take on an apartment, condo or HOA pool before you check whether your state wants a certified operator.
Don't keep pool chemicals in a hot car or beside fuel. Store them dry, cool and apart, as CDC and EPA say.

count.what: HOAs and community managers, real estate agents and storefront shops who could refer people to you

off_season.play: Book next season's installs now with a deposit, while installers have open calendars, and offer to hang and take down lights people already own.

crowd.note: Busy October to January: installs in the fall, takedowns in January. Slow February to August, when you book next season.
not_yet: Don't buy a lift or a truckload of lights before you have booked homes.
Don't add outlets, open a panel or splice into house wiring. That is an electrician's job.
Don't climb a second story before you have ladder practice, a helper and insurance.

count.what: schools, churches and community and rec centers who could refer people to you

crowd.buyer: Parents, and adults who want to learn

off_season.play: Offer a summer block of 6 lessons and book fall times before school starts.

crowd.note: Safety rules with minors come first: parents book, and lessons happen where a parent can see or hear.
not_yet: Don't rent a studio before your weekly schedule is full.
Don't promise exam results, audition spots or a set pace.
Don't message students under 18 directly. Talk to parents.

count.what: apartment buildings, yoga and pilates studios and physical therapy clinics who could refer people to you

crowd.buyer: Adults who want help starting to exercise
crowd.note: Safety first: your certification, CPR and AED training and insurance come before your first client, and the PAR-Q+ before every first session. Expect evening and weekend sessions.
not_yet: Don't train anyone before they've filled in the PAR-Q+ from the PAR-Q+ Collaboration.
Don't take a paying client before your liability insurance is active.
Don't buy equipment before your fifth regular client: bodyweight and a band are enough to start.

count.what: gyms and fitness studios, yoga and pilates studios and churches who could refer people to you

crowd.buyer: Busy families and couples who want home-cooked dinners
crowd.note: Trust first: a free kitchen visit before any cook day. Groceries go on the bill at cost.
not_yet: Don't sell meals cooked in your own kitchen until you've checked your state's cottage food and health rules.
Don't give diet or health advice: cook to what the client tells you.
Don't rent a commercial kitchen before you have 4 regular clients.

count.what: senior and community centers, public libraries and churches who could refer people to you

crowd.note: Trust comes first: the client types every password, family is welcome at every visit, and every visit ends with a written note.
not_yet: Don't offer remote help with screen sharing apps. Help in person.
Don't take on office networks or business IT before your tenth home client.
Don't keep, write down or store anyone's passwords, even when they ask you to.

count.what: wedding and event venues, florists and bakeries who could refer people to you

crowd.note: Weddings peak in spring and fall. Birthdays, showers and work events run all year.
not_yet: Don't take full planning before you've run 5 day-of events.
Don't buy decor, linens or rentals to rent out before your tenth event.
Don't book a date without a signed agreement and a deposit.

count.what: real estate agents, movers and senior living and senior centers who could refer people to you

crowd.buyer: Busy households and people moving or downsizing
crowd.note: Trust first: a free walk-through, the client's yes on every item, and photos only with a written okay.
not_yet: Don't buy bins before the sort and the measuring.
Don't haul, sell or store a client's things in your first month.
Don't take a home with blocked exits, pests or mold on your own.

count.what: property managers, real estate agents and estate sale and consignment shops who could refer people to you

off_season.play: Work move-outs and estate cleanouts with property managers and estate sale shops, and presell spring garage cleanouts at this year's price.

crowd.note: Busiest March to October, peaking April to June (LawnStarter).
not_yet: Don't buy a dump truck or a big trailer before your tenth paid load.
Don't haul paint, chemicals, propane tanks or tires until you know your county's rules.
Don't take a fridge, freezer or AC unit until you know who recovers the refrigerant.

count.what: real estate agents, apartment offices and self storage who could refer people to you

crowd.buyer: People moving locally who rent their own truck or container

off_season.play: Lead with move-outs through apartment offices and senior communities, and sell small jobs: furniture moved inside the home, storage units loaded.

crowd.note: Busiest May to September, and at the start and end of every month.
not_yet: Don't drive a customer's things for pay. Load and unload only, unless you hold the carrier authority and the state license that work needs.
Don't buy a truck. The customer rents it; you bring pads, dollies and straps.
Don't take pianos, safes or pool tables before you have a third mover and an appliance dolly.

count.what: real estate agents, property managers and landlords and apartment buildings who could refer people to you

crowd.note: Handyman work runs all year; spring and fall bring seasonal checkups (Housecall Pro) and the weatherstripping check (Fixr). The busier months are a judgment call.
not_yet: Don't quote panels, new wiring, gas or moved pipes: send those to a licensed trade.
Don't take a job over your state's limit for work without a contractor license until you check the rule.
Don't buy big tools before a job calls for them: rent or borrow the first time.
